name: n04-ipv6struct
title: Structure of an IPv6 address
spec: One long bar split into three segments: 'site prefix 48 bits' + 'subnet ID 16 bits' + 'interface ID 64 bits'. Beneath, the example 2001:0db8:0a0b | 12f0 | 0000:0000:0000:8b6e aligned to the segments (monospace). A bracket over the first two segments 'first 64 bits = the /64 subnet prefix'. Below, nested boxes: ISP/cloud /32 contains site /48 contains 65,536 /64 subnets. Orange note: 'Almost every subnet is a /64'.
cap: A global IPv6 address is a site prefix, a subnet ID and a 64-bit interface ID, and subnets are almost always /64.

name: n04-ipv6types
title: Reading IPv6 address prefixes
spec: Table with two columns, prefix (monospace) and meaning, rows: '::1/128' loopback; '2000::/3' global unicast (begins with 2 or 3); 'fd00::/8' unique local (ULA, private); 'fe80::/10' link-local, valid on one link only; 'ff00::/8' multicast (ff02::1 all nodes, ff02::2 all routers); '2001:db8::/32' documentation; '::ffff:0:0/96' IPv4-mapped; '64:ff9b::/96' NAT64. Orange highlight on the line 'There is no broadcast in IPv6'.
cap: The first digits of an IPv6 address tell you its type, and multicast replaces broadcast.

name: n04-ipv4hdr
title: The IPv4 header
spec: A 32-bit-wide grid, four columns of 8 bits, rows: Row1 Version | IHL | DSCP | ECN | Total Length; Row2 Identification | Flags | Fragment Offset; Row3 TTL | Protocol | Header Checksum; Row4 Source Address; Row5 Destination Address; Row6 Options (rare). Side notes: 'IHL 5 = 20 bytes', 'TTL drops by one at each router', 'Flags: DF and MF'. Orange highlight on Protocol with note '6 = TCP'. Monospace for field names.
cap: The IPv4 header is 20 bytes minimum, with fragmentation fields, TTL and a protocol field.
